task: OC10 tool catalog audit and closed controller metadata release
scope: Only CodemodeController.close changes production behavior. Other changes are existing-test/benchmark extensions and audit documentation.

commands.focused: node --expose-gc --experimental-strip-types --test tests/codemode-session.test.ts tests/codemode-runtime.test.ts tests/codemode-guardrails.test.ts tests/codemode-hot-paths.test.ts tests/tool-selection.test.ts

verification.failure: New MCP schema-refresh assertion initially indexed old cumulative fixture results; test-only index corrected.
verification.baselineFailure: Existing inline-declaration case extended with close assertions: expected identifiers.size=0, actual=100 before production fix.

callChain: CodemodeSandbox registerTool/unregisterTool / execute snapshot and catalog / WorkerData
Worker ALL_TOOLS snapshot / describeTools bridge / CodemodeController.describe
NestedToolDispatcher current-tool lookup and policy / schema validation / MCP adapter
results / read evidence / store / CodemodeController.close / sandbox.close / session disposal

ownership.owner: Session-owned CodemodeController owns descriptors, tool definitions and two name maps; sandbox owns toolsByName/snapshot/catalog. Worker owns a per-execution transferred catalog.
ownership.normalTurns: Measured zero schema property reads and stable descriptor/snapshot/catalog identity; no new per-progress/delta factories. Worker transfer still occurs per script.
lifecycleExemptions: CodemodeController.setTools: explicit registration/selection boundary; wrappers/descriptors/signatures/maps already allocated here
CodemodeController.describe and tool_search.execute: explicit calls with bounded result selection; scans/formatting remain
CodemodeController.close: existing asynchronous disposal boundary; finally now clears maps and description even if sandbox close rejects
CodemodeStore.reset and CodemodeSandbox.close: existing lifecycle cleanup allocation
ownership.closedOwner: Before fix, maps and inline description survive close while owner remains referenced. After fix, counts are zero. Both versions collect once owner is unreferenced.
ownership.arbitraryMutation: Supported updates re-register definitions. Direct in-place mutation bypassing registration is not promised to invalidate cached metadata.
ownership.poolDecision: No object pools, additional caches, engine changes or Worker pooling.
ownership.releaseCoverage: Existing runtime tests cover normal/error/abort and snapshot invalidation; session tests cover reload/branches and close failure; controlled-GC benchmarks cover disposed successful real sessions.

baselineCatalog.coverage: 8/512 registered host tools (MCP names are metadata fixtures); real SDK, controller, describe bridge, compiled Worker and disposal. No real server/model, provider token/cache measurement or Worker heap.

candidateCatalog.coverage: 8/512 registered host tools (MCP names are metadata fixtures); real SDK, controller, describe bridge, compiled Worker and disposal. No real server/model, provider token/cache measurement or Worker heap.

candidateSession.coverage: real SDK, built-in reads, AgentSession policy/hooks/results/store, Worker, projection and disposal; offline provider; excludes UI, worker heap and disk sessions

limitations: Catalog schema 'properties' getter reads are not signature-render call counts; 3 reads occur for one described fixture schema.
Catalog benchmark MCP names are metadata fixtures, not a server. Real McpBridgeRuntime schema replacement, policy and activation use existing session test.
Sampling includes cold session construction and Worker transport; host samples exclude Worker/QuickJS heaps. Single samples are not proof of reduced allocation or speed.
No real provider token/cache metrics, model turn savings, full UI, external MCP server, total heap peak or cross-product performance claims.
Controller-generated signatures may omit or use unknown for complex schemas; current full schema remains the actual input validation boundary.
resources: Existing benchmark/test temp roots are removed in their finally/after cleanup. No persistent services or additional test files.
